question: Why were some claim payments loaded twice in June 2026?

grade.reason: Nothing to find: needs the LLM grader (Phase 3).

report.interpretation: You asked why some claim payments were loaded twice in June 2026. I checked claim_payments for exact duplicates (same claim, date, amount and payee), by payment month and by load batch.
report.answer: The premise is wrong: no payments were loaded twice in June 2026. All 159 duplicated payment rows have payment dates between 2026-03-02 and 2026-03-13. Each one was loaded a second time by a non-nightly batch called 'reload-2026-03-14'. That adds about $893K of double-counted payments to March 2026. June has no duplicates and no rows from non-nightly batches. The data doesn't show why the reload happened. It looks like a manual re-run of the March 2–13 payments that overlapped rows already loaded nightly. Someone in data engineering would need to confirm that.
report.answer_sql: WITH d AS (SELECT claim_id, payment_date, amount, payee_type, count(*) n FROM claim_payments GROUP BY ALL HAVING count(*)>1) SELECT date_trunc('month', payment_date) AS month, sum(n-1) AS extra_rows, sum(amount*(n-1)) AS extra_amount FROM d GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

findings.claim: All 159 duplicate payment rows are in March 2026 and come from the reload-2026-03-14 batch. None are in June 2026.
findings.evidence_sql: WITH d AS (SELECT claim_id, payment_date, amount, payee_type, count(*) n, count(*) FILTER (WHERE load_batch LIKE 'reload%') r FROM claim_payments GROUP BY ALL HAVING count(*)>1) SELECT date_trunc('month', payment_date) AS month, count(*) AS dup_groups, sum(n-1) AS extra_rows, sum(r) AS reload_rows, sum(amount*(n-1)) AS extra_amount FROM d GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

hypotheses.evidence: There are no duplicates and no non-nightly batch rows for June payment dates.

hypotheses.hypothesis: A manual reload on 2026-03-14 re-delivered March 2–13 payments that were already loaded
hypotheses.evidence: All 159 duplicates sit in the reload-2026-03-14 batch and cover payment dates 2026-03-02 to 2026-03-13. The reason for the reload isn't recorded in the data.

data_quality_issues.issue: 159 payment rows duplicated by the reload-2026-03-14 batch, worth about $893K
data_quality_issues.impact: Paid amount and incurred losses for March 2026 are overstated unless the duplicates are excluded. Claims with those payments are affected.

proposed_actions.title: Remove or flag 159 duplicate payments from reload-2026-03-14
proposed_actions.reason: They overstate March 2026 paid amounts by about $893K. Data engineering should also confirm why the reload ran.

open_questions: Did you see a June anomaly in a particular report? If so, tell me which one, and I'll check it. It may come from something other than duplicate loads.
